reference_sql:
SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
  epoch(event_ts) - epoch(LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id)) AS gap_seconds
FROM app_events
WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-26 00:00:00+00'
  AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-27 00:00:00+00'
alternatives:
WITH day_events AS (
  -- one row per app event on 26 October 2025 (UTC)
  SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-26 00:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-27 00:00:00+00'
)
SELECT e.event_id, e.user_id, e.event_ts,
  epoch(e.event_ts) - epoch((SELECT MAX(p.event_ts) FROM day_events p
    WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.event_ts < e.event_ts)) AS gap_seconds
FROM day_events e

SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
  date_diff('second', LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id), event_ts) AS gap_seconds
FROM app_events
WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-26 00:00:00+00'
  AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-27 00:00:00+00'

other_way.sql:
WITH day_events AS (
  -- one row per app event on 26 October 2025 (UTC)
  SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-26 00:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-27 00:00:00+00'
)
SELECT e.event_id, e.user_id, e.event_ts,
  epoch(e.event_ts) - epoch((SELECT MAX(p.event_ts) FROM day_events p
    WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.event_ts < e.event_ts)) AS gap_seconds
FROM day_events e
other_way.tradeoff: A subquery that finds the user's latest earlier event works too, but it searches the day again for every event.
